source.title: Microsoft SQL node: \ inside [bracketed] identifier treated as unbound query parameter

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

The Microsoft SQL node fails on queries that use a bracketed identifier containing `$` followed by digits, even when no query parameters are set. The query never reaches the server:

```
The query references $123, but only 0 query parameter(s) are set
```

Table names like `[Company$Table 1$123-456-789]` are standard in Microsoft Dynamics NAV / Business Central databases, so these workflows broke after the v3 upgrade.

Cause: the unbound placeholder check in `bindQueryParameters` (`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/Sql/GenericFunctions.ts`) skips `$N` inside `'...'` and `"..."` via `isInsideQuotes`, but not inside SQL Server `[...]` identifiers, so `$123` in the table name is read as a parameter reference.

Reported on the community forum: https://community.n8n.io/t/329049

### To Reproduce

1. Add a Microsoft SQL node, operation Execute Query, with no Query Parameters.
2. Query: `SELECT TOP 1 * FROM [Company$Table 1$123-456-789]` (any table whose bracketed name contains `$` followed by digits).
3. Execute the node.
4. See error: `The query references $123, but only 0 query parameter(s) are set`.

Workaround: write the identifier with double quotes instead, e.g. `"Company$Table 1$123-456-789"`.

### Expected behavior

`$N` inside a `[bracketed]` identifier is treated as part of the identifier, as it already is inside quoted strings, and the query runs. A real unbound placeholder outside brackets should still throw.

### Debug Info

Not available from the forum reporter. Reproduced in the node's unit tests against current master; see the linked PR.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (forum reporter)

### n8n Version

3.2

### Node.js Version

Not provided (official Docker image)

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The current helper only tracks single- and double-quoted spans. In `packages/nodes-base/utils/sql-query-parameters.ts`, `isInsideQuotes()` explicitly does not handle SQL comments; in the Microsoft SQL path, the caller also needs to recognize SQL Server bracketed identifiers. A focused fix could extend the lexical scan for `[...]` (including escaped `]]`) and use it when filtering unbound `$N` matches, so `$123` in `[Company$Table 1$123-456-789]` is ignored while placeholders outside the identifier still fail. Please include a case with a closing bracket escaped as `]]` if adding bracket tracking.
